candidate.answerReason: For every real x, x²+1≥1, so A is always a defined square root. B has a negative radicand, C is a cube root, and D requires a≥1.

methods.label: Check root type and radicand
methods.explanation: Since \(x^2+1\ge1>0\), \(\sqrt{x^2+1}\) is always defined. The expression \(\sqrt{-2}\) is undefined, \(\sqrt[3]{3}\) is a cube root expression, and \(\sqrt{a-1}\) is undefined when \(a<1\).
methods.levelReason: Uses nonnegativity of squares, the real square-root condition and recognition of cube-root notation.
